purpose: ForgeFront 美术方向候选；待用户选定，非最终游戏资源

variants.name: a-flat-atlas
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original game art-direction reference screenshot for ForgeFront, a desktop-browser real-time strategy game. Produce a polished wide 16:9 landscape image, ideally 1920x1080. This is a plausible game viewport, not a marketing poster. The map occupies the left 80%, an unobtrusive light contextual barracks panel occupies the right 20%, with a very thin resource header. Nearly top-down orthographic view. An original fictional continuous continent with a hooked western peninsula, a central bay from the south, broad connected northern land bridge, and an eastern promontory. Light blue sea around the edges. All playable land connected, NO detached playable islands. Divide the entire land into approximately 48 small organic irregular province polygons, contiguous without gaps, unequal in shape but comparable in area, fine unobtrusive internal borders. Not regular hexagons, not square tiles, not jigsaw puzzle knobs. World-atlas bright colors, high-key daylight, no dark theme, no parchment sepia.
A mid-game 1v1 state: player holds a compact group in the southwest with teal outlines and translucent teal tint; opponent holds northeast with coral outlines and translucent coral tint; neutral land retains pale green and warm cream. Only two factions. Terrain remains visible beneath ownership. Selected player barracks province gets a clear bright outline. Show small modern industrial barracks, workshops and gold mine icons with distinct silhouettes, modest garrison counters, restrained supply lines linking some friendly buildings, fine green lines with white moving-dot marks, blue rivers distinct from routes, one small contested frontier with tiny battle symbol. Mountains and forest decoration must not hide province borders or look like impassable walls.
Right sidebar: pale ivory/navy labels, compact selected barracks vignette, garrison 42/60, two small equipment slots, two blueprint cards, a production progress bar, concise English labels only: FORGEFRONT, GOLD, TROOPS, BARRACKS, GARRISON, SUPPLY, BLUEPRINTS, TRAIN. No large decorative prose, no pause button, no next-turn button, no minimap, no elaborate invented systems. UI should be readable and modest; map is the hero.
Reference the broad visual principles of OpenFront territory clarity, Civilization VI inviting readable terrain, and Hearts of Iron strategic province/frontline cartography without copying any actual map, trademark, existing UI, national flag, or historical insignia. No logos or watermarks. Not pixel art. Designed as an achievable 2D/2.5D visual target for a small independent game.
VARIANT A — CLEAN FLAT WORLD ATLAS. Flat vector-like cartographic rendering, crisp elegant coastlines, almost no shadows, very subtle paper-free grain. Pastel light-blue ocean #B9E1ED, mint plains #DAE8C3, cream dry land #F0DFB4, teal #368D91 and coral #D47C72 faction accents, slate navy typography. Tiny flat silhouette trees and simple contour strokes for hills. Buildings are compact flat map symbols, not 3D miniatures. Province outlines hairline warm gray; faction outlines stronger. Flat pale cards in the right panel, simple line icons. Highest legibility and generous breathing room. The visual focus is province topology and territory control, akin to a beautiful contemporary school world atlas. One complete screenshot, no comparison grid, no title badge.
Important: show GOLD 1240 and TROOPS 386 only in the header. Infantry equipment only: machine gun, sniper rifle, rocket launcher, flamethrower; no tanks or armored vehicles, no new unit types. Target about 48 provinces, not hundreds of tiny areas. Keep country-scale territory readable.

Friendly lightly painterly 2.5D miniature terrain inspired by Civilization VI's readable sculpted landforms, but rendered as restrained top-down illustration suitable for 2D sprites. Soft low mountain ridges with snowy tips, small forest clusters, bright grassland, pale sandy patches, pale turquoise shallow water and blue open sea, a few delicate contour lines. Low relief, extremely soft ambient shadows, no dramatic perspective. Small stylized industrial building miniatures with light walls and teal roofs, warm stone gold mines. Province boundaries remain continuously legible OVER terrain; no hex grid. Pale modern right panel with a small illustrated barracks thumbnail, understated teal controls. Keep typography and icons clean. Saturated enough to feel sunny, muted enough for strategic clarity. One complete screenshot, no comparison grid, no title badge.

Pale sky-blue water, light pistachio land, warm cream uplands; translucent teal and muted coral ownership fields. Small flat rectangular NATO-inspired generic unit counters (simple non-historical symbols) and sparse garrison numerals. Emphasize a short restrained teal/coral frontline at the center, one thin directional attack arrow, clean green dotted supply links, small numbered industrial icons.
